Aminata Diallo is a young woman living in a rented room in a bustling district on the outskirts of Bamako. She keeps a small notebook of figures and dates tucked inside her shirt and maintains an emergency fund hidden under a loose floorboard near her mattress, adding the same amount each month and never touching it in daylight.

Her background includes a long-standing practice of careful accounting, precision, and self-reliance. She learned to double-check and count everything after watching her mother lose a market stall to a miscalculated loan, and after her mother died when Aminata was twelve she continued to count bricks, costs, steps, and weeks with habitual exactness. She values careful recordkeeping, restraint, and practical reliability, and she does not speak about plans openly because she has learned that spoken plans can be borrowed against.
